title: Sequence-lattice bucketer + prefill prioritizer for pad reduction
creator: Rishi Patel
description:
Problem: Our serving runtime still pays a significant pad tax for workloads with high variance in request sequence lengths. Existing bucketers create relatively coarse bins and the scheduler treats prefill and decode uniformly, which leaves room for pad reduction and cheaper kernel selection.

Proposal: Implement a sequence-lattice bucketer combined with a prefill-priority scheduler. The lattice bucketer constructs overlapping, hierarchical buckets (a lattice) across seqlen ranges such that each request can be mapped to the smallest compatible bucket without excessive fragmentation. The prefill-priority scheduler biases packing towards prefill-dominant microbatches and defers low-impact short decodes into opportunistic slots. Together this reduces padded tokens and enables more efficient kernel selection (select narrower attention kernels, fuse KV consolidation, and prefer sparse-friendly kernels when occupancy is low).

Key components to deliver: 1) Lattice bucketer algorithm + runtime mapping API (non-blocking, fast path). 2) Prefill-priority microbatch scheduler that marks packets as PREFILL / DECODE / HYBRID and exposes priorities to the kernel-hint layer. 3) Kernel-hint plumbing: runtime provides expected occupancy and attention window to the kernel selector so it can pick optimized kernels (grouped attention, block-sparse when applicable, or high-throughput narrow-kernel). 4) KV consolidation for coalesced prefill requests to reduce memory churn. 5) End-to-end telemetry and perf regression tests.

Why this is different: Instead of rigid fixed-width buckets, the lattice supports fine-grained grouping while keeping packing overhead and fragmentation low. Combining scheduling signals (prefill vs decode) with kernel hints unlocks more deterministic kernel choices and avoids worst-case latency spike when mixed workloads collide.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end lattice bucketer compiles and passes unit tests for bucket placement and eviction
Scheduler can label and prioritize PREFILL packets and produce microbatches with less than 10% increased variance in wait time
End-to-end synthetic benchmark shows >=12% token pad reduction on mixed-length public traces (and >=8% cost reduction on 2 representative customer workloads)
No percentile latency regression >5ms P99 on small-model throughput targets and P50 latency improves or stays flat
Kernel selector uses occupancy hint for at least 3 kernel codepaths (narrow-attn, grouped-attn, generic) with telemetry proving correct choices
notes: We will reuse the existing bucket histogram primitives from ENG-9142 for seqlen distribution estimates
Initial prototype uses static lattice tiers: [1-16, 8-32, 24-64, 48-128, 96-256] with overlap to allow small-fit mapping
Kernel-hint surface is intentionally minimal: {expected_seq_len, avg_batch_occupancy, prefill_ratio} - expressed as simple enums/ints to keep selector cheap
Memory safety: KV consolidation will be limited to batches < N_kv_bytes to avoid page thrashing. N_kv_bytes will be an operator-configurable knob
Telemetry: add metrics pad_tokens_saved, batches_with_prefill_bias, kernel_hint_mismatch_count to console dashboard
Risk: heavyweight scheduler heuristics could increase tail latency if not bounded; we will run closed-loop canary with canary_ratio=2% and rollout ramping
comments: 2026-03-01 - Rishi Patel: Kickoff. Drafted lattice bucketer design and trade-offs. Decided to prototype with overlapping static tiers rather than fully dynamic tiers to get iteration speed.

2026-03-03 - Lena Torres: Implemented the mapping function and added unit tests for overlap resolution. Observed 18% pad reduction in a unit trace but increased variance in microbatch waiting time (investigating).

2026-03-05 - QA: Added synthetic traces from two customers (analytics-chat, doc-summarization). Initial results: 12% and 9% pad reduction respectively, cost delta computed using per-token GPU time estimates.
2026-03-06 - Design review (Jae Kim): Suggested exposing prefill flag at RPC header so upper layers can hint intent early. Approved approach; added a follow-up to update SDK header mapping.

2026-03-08 - Engineering review (Samira Ortiz): Raised concern about kernel-hint explosion. Decision: keep hints narrow and have selector fall back gracefully to generic kernel if mismatch count grows. Added telemetry for mismatch monitoring.

2026-03-10 - Lena Torres: Kernel hint plumbing wired to selector. Benchmarked three kernels: narrow-attn improved throughput by 22% on high-occupancy batches; grouped-attn helped when occupancy < 40% for long-context workloads.

2026-03-12 - Performance: Collected canary metrics. Pad tokens saved stable at ~14% on mixed traffic in us-west1 test cluster. P99 latency unchanged vs baseline. Plan to open PR and invite perf team for a 48h soak test.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (week 1): Prototype lattice mapping + unit tests + simple scheduler that greedily packs small prefills into lattice buckets
Phase 2 (week 2): Kernel-hint API and selector integration; add KV consolidation path for prefills
Phase 3 (week 3): Canary rollout with telemetry, run 48h soak, compare pad savings/cost-benefit and tail latency; iterate heuristics
Phase 4 (week 4): SDK header updates, docs, runbook, and rollout to 25% then 100% following SRE gating
next_steps: Open feature PR for lattice bucketer (current branch: feature/lattice-bucketer)
Add prefills-as-header to SDK; coordinate with SDK team (owner: Miguel Alvarez)
Schedule perf team 48h soak test and invite SRE for rollout gating
